pr.title: promotion: don't promote int::MIN / -1
pr.description:
Looks like I entirely forgot about this case when adding the div-by-zero check, which was supposed to ensure that we never promote operations that can fail...
Cc https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/80619

This is a breaking change, so needs a crater run.
r? @oli-obk
pr.author: RalfJung

analysis.summary: Fix PromoteTemps so integral `Div`/`Rem` is not promoted merely because the divisor is a known nonzero constant: signed `int::MIN / -1` and `int::MIN % -1` remain fallible and must stay unpromoted. The historical validator only checked for a nonzero RHS and missed the signed-overflow case.
analysis.originalLogic: In `promote_consts.rs`, `Validator` handles `BinOp::Div | BinOp::Rem` for an integral LHS by requiring the RHS to be a known nonzero constant. The pre-fix code evaluated the RHS with `try_eval_bits` and accepted it when `Some(x) if x != 0 => {}`, otherwise returned `Err(Unpromotable)`. The surrounding comment states: `// Integer division: the RHS must be a non-zero const.` and `// The remaining operations can never fail.` This was intended to ensure: "we never promote operations that can fail".
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The incorrect historical transformation promoted an integral division/remainder when the RHS was any known nonzero constant, including `-1`, even when the signed LHS was the minimum value for its type. Thus expressions such as `&(i32::MIN / -1)`, `&(i32::MIN / (0-1))`, `&(-128i8 / -1)`, and the corresponding `% -1` forms were treated as promotable constants instead of remaining temporary values. That transformation is wrong because signed `MIN / -1` and `MIN % -1` overflow and can panic. The corrected transformation adds a signed check: when the RHS is `-1` (or unknown), the LHS must be a known constant that is not `signed_int_min`; otherwise the operation is `Unpromotable`. A two-program differential can keep the same operation and only change the LHS constant, e.g. `&(i32::MIN + 1) / -1` (safe/promotable) versus `&(i32::MIN) / -1` (must not be promoted), or change the RHS `0-1` versus another nonzero divisor.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR const-promotion candidates containing an integral `BinOp::Div` or `BinOp::Rem` whose operands are constants or fold to constants. Relevant types are signed integers (`i8`, `i16`, `i32`, `i64`, `i128`, `isize`), especially the type minimum divided or remaindered by `-1`, including divisors written as constant expressions like `(0-1)`. The domain also includes safe boundary cases that must remain promotable: nonzero divisors such as `1`, `-1` with a non-minimum LHS, `i32::MIN / 1`, `1 % 1`, and unsigned divisions/remainders. Zero divisors and unknown divisors belong to the pre-existing unpromotable path.
analysis.trigger: The trigger is a signed integral `Div` or `Rem` promotion candidate where the RHS evaluates to `-1` (directly or by constant folding) and the LHS evaluates to that type's minimum value; equivalently, `lhs_ty.is_signed()` and the divisor is `-1` or unknown while the LHS is unknown or equals `sz.signed_int_min()`. The historical bug fires because the nonzero-divisor check alone accepts this case.
preconditions: Const promotion is considering an integral `BinOp::Div` or `BinOp::Rem` expression.
The operation's LHS and RHS are available as constants to the promotion validator (or the RHS can be constant-evaluated), allowing the fallibility check to inspect them.
The type is signed and the divisor is `-1` (or constant-folds to `-1`), with the dividend equal to the signed minimum for that type.
Under the historical logic, the RHS is a known nonzero constant, so the operation is accepted as promotable despite the signed-overflow case.
pitfalls: Do not limit the fix to `Div`; the same patch handles `BinOp::Rem`, and tests include `i8::MIN % -1` through `isize::MIN % -1`.
Do not treat every division by `-1` as unpromotable: `1/-1` and `0/1` are added as promotable safe cases, and `i32::MIN/1` is also promotable.
The RHS need not be literally `-1`; `(0-1)` constant-folds to `-1`, and the regression test `i32::MIN/(0-1)` must remain unpromoted.
The check must be type-size-aware: `-128i8 / -1` is the `i8` minimum case, just as `i32::MIN / -1` is the `i32` case.

The pre-existing zero-divisor test used bit evaluation; the signed check needs integer interpretation and `sz.signed_int_min()`. The patch switched to `try_eval_scalar_int` and uses `try_to_uint` for the zero test (`// for the zero test, int vs uint does not matter`) and `try_to_int` for the signed test.
Do not over-promote `1/0`, `1/(1-1)`, or `(1+1)/(1-1)`; the RHS must be known nonzero before the signed MIN/-1 check is relevant.

Do not expect the lint test to report both the overflow-panic lint and an `E0080` constant-evaluation failure; the patch removes the duplicate `evaluation of constant value failed` expectations for the referenced `MIN / -1` and `MIN % -1` cases.
analysis.testStrategy: Use `tests/ui/consts/promote-not.rs` to assert that fallible signed MIN/-1 operations are not promoted: borrowing `&(i32::MIN/-1)`, `&(i32::MIN/(0-1))`, `&(-128i8/-1)`, and analogous expressions into `&'static _` must produce `E0716` (`temporary value dropped while borrowed`). Use `tests/ui/consts/promotion.rs` to assert that safe boundary cases still promote via `assert_static`, including `&(1/1)`, `&(0/1)`, `&(1/-1)`, `&(i32::MIN/1)`, and `&(1%1)`. Use `tests/ui/lint/lint-overflowing-ops.rs` with `//~ ERROR: this operation will panic at runtime` for `&(i8::MIN / -1)` through `&(isize::MIN / -1)` and the corresponding remainder cases, while removing the old `evaluation of constant value failed` annotations. Compare noopt, opt, and opt-with-overflow-checks stderr variants for consistent diagnostics. No compiler execution or reproduction is claimed here; these are regression-test expectations present in the patch.
evidence: Looks like I entirely forgot about this case when adding the div-by-zero check, which was supposed to ensure that we never promote operations that can fail...
// Integer division: the RHS must be a non-zero const.
_ => return Err(Unpromotable), // value not known or 0 -- not okay
// Furthermore, for signed divison, we also have to exclude `int::MIN / -1`.
// The RHS is -1 or unknown, so we have to be careful.
_ => return Err(Unpromotable), // value not known or int::MIN -- not okay
let _val: &'static _ = &(i32::MIN/-1); //~ ERROR temporary value dropped while borrowed
let _val: &'static _ = &(i32::MIN/(0-1)); //~ ERROR temporary value dropped while borrowed
let _val: &'static _ = &(-128i8/-1); //~ ERROR temporary value dropped while borrowed
// div-by-non-0 (and also not MIN/-1) is okay
